cases.name: recipe
text: watch|29 psi wants attention paid to the compression ratio, the fuel and the intercooler, not just to the turbocharger.

note|Pump petrol at this boost is the limit worth thinking about. E85 buys knock margin cheaply — see the Octane calculator — at the cost of about half again the fuel, which the injectors and pump below already account for if you change the fuel here.

cases.name: recipe
text: stop|42 psi is a great deal of boost. Before buying anything, see whether more displacement, more engine speed or better filling gets there on less — every part of this list gets cheaper when the boost comes down.
watch|325 hp per litre is a serious specific output. It is done, but not on standard internals and not for long on pump fuel.

cases.name: recipe
text: stop|31.5 m/s of mean piston speed at 11,000 rpm is race-engine territory, where rods and rings are consumables. Either the speed comes down or the parts stop being production ones.

stop|63 psi is a great deal of boost. Before buying anything, see whether more displacement, more engine speed or better filling gets there on less — every part of this list gets cheaper when the boost comes down.
watch|700 hp per litre is a serious specific output. It is done, but not on standard internals and not for long on pump fuel.

note|Pump petrol at this boost is the limit worth thinking about. E85 buys knock margin cheaply — see the Octane calculator — at the cost of about half again the fuel, which the injectors and pump below already account for if you change the fuel here.

cases.name: recipe
text: stop|31.9 m/s of mean piston speed at 7,000 rpm is race-engine territory, where rods and rings are consumables. Either the speed comes down or the parts stop being production ones.
note|This target needs no boost at all — the engine can breathe it naturally. The turbocharger below is what it would take if the filling were worse than assumed.

cases.name: recipe
text: watch|27 psi wants attention paid to the compression ratio, the fuel and the intercooler, not just to the turbocharger.

watch|At 1,200 rpm this engine wants 8 lb/min, which is 14% of what the G25-660 is rated for. That is near the left of its map, where it will be slow to come up and may surge. A smaller turbocharger, or two of them, would spool where you want it.

cases.name: recipe
text: stop|39 psi is a great deal of boost. Before buying anything, see whether more displacement, more engine speed or better filling gets there on less — every part of this list gets cheaper when the boost comes down.
note|The torque peak is at or above the power peak, which no engine does. The spool check below means nothing until those are the right way round.
watch|267 hp per litre is a serious specific output. It is done, but not on standard internals and not for long on pump fuel.

note|Pump petrol at this boost is the limit worth thinking about. E85 buys knock margin cheaply — see the Octane calculator — at the cost of about half again the fuel, which the injectors and pump below already account for if you change the fuel here.

cases.name: spray_flow
text: Twice methanol's cooling per pound and no fuel value at all, so a big spray does not enrich anything — which cuts both ways: it cools best and it is the one that leans the mixture if you were relying on the spray. Freezes, so it is a poor choice anywhere that gets cold, and needs something in it to stop the pump corroding.
